findings.expected: Single canonical deja-vu version across sh wrapper, ps1 wrapper, and governance doc.
findings.impact: Non-deterministic MCP memory runtime depending on OS entry point; governance doc drift.
findings.root_cause: Independent per-OS/per-doc version updates without a single source of truth.
findings.remediation: Choose one canonical version; sync both wrappers and mcp-governance.md.

findings.expected: All MCP wrappers pin explicit versions (as context7@3.2.4, filesystem@2026.1.14, neo4j-server@0.2.0 do).
findings.actual: Mixed policy: several wrappers use bare `npx -y <pkg>` resolving to latest.
findings.impact: Non-reproducible MCP runtime; silent supply-chain upgrade risk. Local runtime (not production CI) => P2.
findings.root_cause: Inconsistent pin policy across MCP wrappers.
findings.remediation: Pin listed packages to verified versions in both .sh and .ps1.
validation: for f in scripts/ai/mcp/*.sh scripts/ai/mcp/*.ps1; do rg -o 'npx -y [^"']*' "$f"; done

evidence.observation: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'psutil' at import time
psutil>=5.9 IS declared as a dependency

findings.expected: memory workflow smoke runs in a properly provisioned env.
findings.actual: Smoke failed only because the ad-hoc system python3 lacked psutil; psutil is declared in pyproject.toml, so this is an environment provisioning gap, not a code defect.
findings.impact: None on product; audit-env limitation. Memory smoke NOT validated this iteration.
findings.root_cause: Audit ran with unprovisioned system interpreter (no project venv on this host).
findings.remediation: Re-run smoke inside project venv (.venv-win on Windows) to confirm memory tooling.
